item.title: Info minister: Youth key to advancing civilization in AI era
item.description:
Information and Broadcasting Minister Zahir Uddin Swapon said on Wednesday that the youth are the main driving force of new civilization in the era of rapidly changing technology.
“With the knowledge and experience of the old days, it is difficult to deal with the new challenges that are being created every day in the ongoing new ecosystem, including emergence of artificial intelligence (AI). So, it is the duty of every country to impart the right knowledge and skills to the youths,” he said.
The minister was addressing an event at the Foreign Service Academy here marking the “International Youth Day 2026”. The Ministry of Youth and Sports and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs jointly organized the meeting.
The day was celebrated with the theme “2026- Different Contexts, Common Aspirations”. State Minister for Youth and Sports Md Aminul Haque presided over the meeting.
Speaking as the chief guest, Swapon said the unprecedented development of technology, including AI, is a great blessing for human civilization, but it has also brought about completely new challenges.
“The evolution of technology and knowledge is happening so rapidly that it is difficult to predict what will be the next”, he said.
Noting that knowledge is no longer a fixed or static thing as it is constantly being changed, he said the older generation needs to understand that the biological and innate ability to adapt to this new ecosystem is highest among the younger generation.
Stressing the need for enhancing the skills of the youth, he said new technology-based crises are being added to old problems such as employment, food security, natural disasters and climate change.
However, Swapon said, proper institutional system to provide this new technology-based knowledge to the youth has not yet taken a complete shape globally.
International organizations, including the United Nations, should focus on the process of transforming this new knowledge and acquiring skills with the youth as the main focus, he said.
Mentioning the leadership of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, Swapon said the prime minister has proven through various steps of the government that he has full confidence in the capabilities of the youths.
The government is taking positive and visionary decisions to promote sports, develop creativity and involve the youth in addressing global challenges like environment and climate change, he said.
Young entrepreneurs, students and youth representatives from various professions, senior officials of the Ministry of Youths and Sports and the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and foreign guests were present.

item.title: DB vows quick arrests over Tk12.125cr petrol pump robbery
item.description:
The Dhaka Metropolitan Police’s Detective Branch (DB) is working to arrest those responsible for the robbery of Tk12.125 crore from DL Petrol Pump in Uttara while the money was being taken to a bank for deposit.
Additional Police Commissioner (Detective) Mohammad Shafiqul Islam said the suspects would be brought to justice soon.
He made the remarks in response to questions from journalists at the DMP Media Centre on Wednesday afternoon.
“We are all working on this. We are looking into many aspects of the case. We are hopeful that we will apprehend the suspects soon,” Shafiqul Islam said.
He added: “The DB has successfully solved almost all the incidents that have taken place in Dhaka Metropolitan City, and the suspects have been arrested. We are hopeful that we will also solve the robbery involving Tk12.125 crore and bring those responsible to justice.”
The robbery took place between 10am and 10:30am on August 9, when Tk12.125 crore belonging to DL Petrol Pump was being taken to a bank for deposit near the southern side of RAB-1 Battalion headquarters in Uttara.
The petrol pump is reportedly owned by Tasin Akter Haque, a cousin of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman.
According to police and relevant sources, several people riding three motorcycles intercepted the vehicle carrying the money. They rammed the vehicle, forcing it to stop, then threatened the occupants with sharp weapons, snatched bags containing the money and fled the scene.
The case statement identifies the stolen money as belonging to DL Petrol Pump. The petrol pump’s manager, Karim, filed a case with police, naming unidentified individuals as the accused.
People associated with the petrol pump said it handles transactions worth around Tk45-50 lakh a day. Under its usual procedure, the previous day’s sales proceeds are taken to the bank for deposit between 10am and 10:30am the following morning.
As banks remain closed on Fridays and Saturdays, the proceeds from those two days are deposited together on Sunday, the next working day. As a result, a comparatively large amount of money was being transported to the bank that day.

item.title: Rizvi: Koko’s death was an expression of political revenge
item.description:
BNP Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi on Wednesday described the circumstances surrounding the death of Arafat Rahman Koko as “extremely heartbreaking and tragic,” saying he could recall no greater tragedy than a mother having to hold the body of her son and calling it an expression of political revenge.
He made the remarks after offering Fateha and placing floral wreaths at the grave Koko, younger son of BNP founder and late president Ziaur Rahman and former prime minister Khaleda Zia, at Banani graveyard in the morning, marking Koko’s 57th birth anniversary.
Rizvi said he died in an extremely difficult environment and at a time when the country was witnessing “ultimate manifestation of fascism.”
“Koko could no longer cope with the situation. He was suffering from heart disease and was sick. In that situation he died of cardiac arrest,” Rizvi said.
Referring to Khaleda Zia’s confinement when Koko’s body was brought back to Bangladesh, Rizvi said she was being kept under blockade with trucks loaded with sand and timber.
“She had an injury to her eye and had undergone an eye operation. At that very moment, pepper spray was used to make her even more sick while she was being kept confined. And at that very moment, the body of her son was placed in her lap,” he said.
“I cannot recall any tragic event in the world comparable to this. This tragedy surpassed all other tragedies, the body of a son in his mother’s lap. It was an expression of revenge,” Rizvi said.
He accused ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina of using every possible means to harass Zia family and erase its presence and popularity among people. “She tarnished their image, spread propaganda and lies, not a single one of which she could prove,” he said.
Rizvi said Hasina had done so to serve her desire for absolute dominance and to remain in power. “There was nothing Sheikh Hasina did not do to destroy this family of the Liberation War,” he said.
Rizvi claimed Hasina’s family had no contribution to the Liberation War and said her father and she herself had stayed under the patronage and protection of the Pakistani ruling authorities.
“Why this revenge? Because Ziaur Rahman declared independence? Because his wife and two sons remained imprisoned because of that declaration of independence?” he asked.
He said Hasina could never tolerate Ziaur Rahman’s patriotism and popularity among people and therefore subjected his family to repeated suffering.
Rizvi said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, Ziaur Rahman and Khaleda Zia’s elder son, had also been subjected to physical torture and later went to London for treatment.
“What has happened today? Sheikh Hasina had to flee after being chased by people. Today that Tarique Rahman is the prime minister. He is an extremely popular prime minister,” Rizvi said.
Highlighting Koko’s role as a sports organizer, Rizvi said Koko had worked for the development of sports and wanted the state and government to create opportunities for those who would make sports their profession and livelihood.
State Minister for Youth and Sports and Dhaka North City BNP convener Aminul Haque, Dhaka North City BNP member secretary Mostafa Zaman, joint convener and MP SM Jahangir, Dhaka North City BNP member Rezaur Karim Fahim, and Bangladesh Cricket Board director Israfil Khasru, among others, were present.

item.title: Metro rail: More trips at night soon, longer service hours likely from Sept
item.description:
Rabiul Islam works at a restaurant next to Bangladesh Medical University in Shahbagh, Dhaka. Every day, he takes the last metro rail train to Farmgate. But he has to struggle with the crowds. If he fails to board the train for any reason, he faces considerable difficulty finding a bus or other mode of transport.

Rabiul Islam told Prothom Alo that his home in Purba Rajabazar is just a short distance from Farmgate station. “There is no easier way to commute than this. Extending the service or operating hours later into the night would benefit me and all other passengers,” he said.

Rabiul’s experience is consistent with the metro rail authority’s figures. Since 7 June, metro rail services at night have been extended by 20 minutes in both directions. However, the final train operates with a 20-minute gap, resulting in heavy crowds.

The addition of two trains has increased passenger traffic by around 10,000. In response, the metro rail authority has taken steps to add two more trains.

The additional trains are expected to begin operating toward the end of this month. As a result, the current 20-minute gap between the final trains will be reduced to seven or eight minutes.

The Dhaka Mass Transit Company Limited (DMTCL) is responsible for constructing and operating the metro rail system in Dhaka.

According to sources at the organisation, authorities are considering extending metro rail operating hours by another 20 to 30 minutes from September.

If implemented, the last train would depart at 11:00pm. Preparations for this have already been made, the sources said.

DMTCL officials said extending services at night would require more train operators. Recruitment of operators has already been completed, and they are currently undergoing training. Their training will end on 26 August, after which they will begin operating trains. Officials are also examining how maintenance and other preparations can be carried out if services are extended further into the night.

At present, the last train from Motijheel toward Uttara departs at 10:30pm, while the final train from Uttara departs at 9:50pm. The first metro rail train of the day leaves Uttara for Motijheel at 6:30am, while the first train from Motijheel toward Uttara departs at 7:15am. The relevant source said there are currently no plans to extend metro rail operating hours in the morning.

DMTCL officials said the metro rail authority has the capacity to operate one train every three and a half minutes. The original project plan had also envisaged metro rail services running from morning until midnight. However, this was not possible because of a shortage of manpower. Operating hours are now being extended gradually.

According to projections, around 500,000 passengers were expected to travel between Uttara and Motijheel every day. Currently, around 450,000 passengers use the metro rail on average each day. Work is underway to extend the metro rail line to Kamalapur. The extended section may open next year, when daily passenger numbers are expected to rise to 677,000.

Metro rail services in Dhaka began on 28 December 2022. Initially, trains operated between Uttara and Agargaon. Stations were added gradually, and all stations up to Motijheel began allowing passengers to board and disembark on the final day of 2023.

Mohammad Nazrul Islam, director (operations and maintenance) of DMTCL, told Prothom Alo that a decision had been made to add two trains at night. The date will be finalised soon. He said the gap between trains would also be reduced once the additional trains begin operating. He added that work is also underway to extend metro rail operating hours at night from next month.

item.title: Savar police neutralise a bomb contained within a pressure cooker
item.description:
A bomb placed inside a pressure cooker at a mosque ground in the Sadhapur area of Savar, Dhaka, was defused.

The Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Bomb Disposal Unit defused the bomb at around 3:30pm.

A loud explosion was heard from a distance, and white smoke was seen rising into the sky.

Sub-Inspector (SI) Imran Hossain, in charge of the Bhabanipur Police Camp in Savar, told Prothom Alo that the DMP Bomb Disposal Unit arrived at the scene at around 1:45pm. They defused the bomb at 3:28pm.

Earlier, around 1:30am on Tuesday night, local residents found a blue plastic drum at the premises of Laltek Ghora Mosque at Goper Bari in Sadhapur.

Inside the drum was a pressure cooker wrapped in black Scotch tape. Local residents later took the pressure cooker out of the drum, placed it on the mosque ground and informed the police.

SI Imran Hossain said police went to the scene at around 8am after being informed and found the pressure cooker wrapped in black Scotch tape. The Bomb Disposal Unit was then informed.

Police, quoting several locals, said three unidentified people had left the plastic drum at the mosque ground at night. However, it was not immediately known who they were.

The DMP Bomb Disposal Unit arrived at the scene at around 1:45pm and later defused the bomb.

Abdur Rahman, a local resident, told Prothom Alo, “We had been moved away from the area. After waiting for sometime, we heard a loud bang from the bomb blast. We saw smoke rising into the sky.”

item.title: HSC admission: No entry test, applications likely from 15 Sept
item.description:
Applications for admission to Class 11 at the higher secondary level for the upcoming academic year may begin on 15 September.

The admission process is expected to be completed by 10 November, with classes scheduled to begin on 12 November.

As in previous years, students will be admitted based on their SSC and equivalent examination results, with no admission test.

Applications will be submitted online through a centralised system, and admissions will be conducted based on merit and students’ order of preference.

SSC, equivalent results published: Pass rate 64.05pc, 106,009 obtain GPA-5

Professor Syed Akhtaruzzaman, chairman of the Dhaka Education Board, told Prothom Alo that according to the draft schedule, applications are scheduled to open on 15 September.

The schedule will be sent to the Ministry of Education tomorrow, Thursday. If approved, the admission process will begin accordingly.

The results of this year’s SSC and equivalent examinations were published on 10 August. A total of 18,29,485 students took the SSC and equivalent examinations under 11 education boards this year. Of them, 11,38,877 students passed. Nearly 7,00,000 students failed. As a result, more than half of the available seats are expected to remain vacant this year.

There are around 2.5 million seats available for Class 11 admission at colleges and madrasas across the country. Last year, 58.7 per cent of the total seats were filled, leaving 41.3 per cent vacant. This year’s pass rate has fallen further, meaning an even larger number of seats are likely to remain vacant.

SSC result re-scrutiny begins: How to apply, as outlined by education boards

Despite the large number of vacant seats, many students who earned GPA-5 may still be unable to secure admission to their preferred institutions, as comparatively better institutions have fewer seats. More than 116,000 students earned GPA-5 across the 11 education boards this year. Of them, 106,009 students received GPA-5 under the nine general education boards.

Around 1.36 million Class 11 seats to remain vacant

For the past several years, students have been admitted to Class 11 based on their SSC and equivalent examination results. Under the system, students seeking admission must apply online, listing a minimum of five and a maximum of 10 colleges or equivalent educational institutions in order of preference after paying the prescribed fee.

Students are then nominated for admission to an institution based on their results, quota status where applicable, and order of preference.

SSC Results: 1.36m seats in Class 11 to remain vacant

This system is used for admissions to colleges and madrasas only. Admissions to institutions under the Technical Education Board are conducted through a separate process. Apart from a few institutions, including Dhaka’s Notre Dame College, almost all colleges and madrasas in the country use this system for Class 11 admissions.

The Dhaka Education Board conducts the centralised online admission process with technical assistance from Bangladesh University of Engineering and Technology (BUET).

item.title: TIB flags concerns over govt-approved human rights laws
item.description:
Transparency International Bangladesh (TIB) has expressed concern over the Cabinet’s in-principle approval of the draft National Human Rights Commission Act, 2026, and the draft Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Act, 2026, saying key recommendations from stakeholders have been ignored.
The anti-graft watchdog questioned whether the government and ruling party had learned lessons from the enforced disappearances, killings and other human rights violations committed under the previous regime.
In a statement on Wednesday, TIB Executive Director Dr Iftekharuzzaman said several positive provisions had been incorporated into the two draft laws, but provisions that could undermine the independence and effectiveness of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) had been retained.
He said Section 18 of the 2009 NHRC Act had been retained, requiring the commission to rely on reports from the government or heads of the respective forces when investigating allegations of human rights violations by law enforcement agencies.
According to Iftekharuzzaman, this had previously hindered the commission’s ability to ensure accountability for violations committed by law enforcement agencies.
He also raised concerns over the proposed composition of the selection committee for appointing the NHRC chairperson and commissioners, saying government representatives would retain significant influence over the appointments.
TIB also criticized the absence of mandatory provisions ensuring women, minorities and other disadvantaged groups are represented on the five-member commission.
The organization said civil society had proposed that at least two of the five commissioners be women and one be from a small ethnic group, in line with international standards on pluralistic representation.
Iftekharuzzaman further questioned whether the commission would be genuinely independent despite the draft describing it as an independent and impartial institution.
He pointed to provisions requiring prior government approval to establish offices outside Dhaka, allowing up to 30% of employees to be appointed on deputation, and permitting serving government officials to become commissioners on deputation.
“These provisions would effectively turn the Human Rights Commission into a government institution,” he said, questioning whether such an institution was what the July uprising had aspired to.
TIB also expressed concern over the removal of a provision from the earlier draft stating that acting solely on the orders or instructions of a government or superior authority could not be used as an excuse for human rights violations.
The organization also questioned the exclusion of military detention centres from the NHRC’s mandate to conduct regular inspections without prior notice.
Regarding the draft Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Redress Act, Iftekharuzzaman said responsibility for investigating enforced disappearance cases had been placed entirely with the police, excluding the NHRC from the process.
He questioned the effectiveness of a provision under which a junior investigating officer would prepare an interim report when a senior official is accused of involvement in an enforced disappearance.
TIB said the definition of enforced disappearance in the draft also failed to include the possible involvement of elected representatives, ministers and other senior state officials, despite Bangladesh’s experience and relevant international conventions.
The organization further noted that several safeguards and monitoring functions included in the Enforced Disappearances Prevention and Redress Ordinance, 2025, including inspections of detention facilities and efforts to identify secret detention centres, had not been retained in the new draft.
TIB said a significant section of Bangladesh’s population, including members of both ruling and opposition parties, had suffered because of the absence of an independent human rights commission and effective legal safeguards against enforced disappearance.
It urged the government to revise both draft laws before placing them before Parliament, taking into account the views of victims and stakeholders and ensuring that the legislation reflects principles of human rights, accountability and justice.

item.title: CNG crisis: Long queues, limited supply leave Dhaka drivers struggling
item.description:
Long queues, closed filling stations and limited gas supplies have left CNG-run auto-rickshaw and private car drivers scrambling for fuel across Dhaka, with many spending hours at stations for just Tk20-100 worth of gas.
The shortage was particularly acute in Badda, Tejgaon and areas along the airport road on Wednesday.
Jaman CNG station in Merul Badda was closed, with a notice saying there was no CNG. The station in Middle Badda was also without gas.
Of several stations from Kuril Bishwaroad to the airport, only the one in Khilkhet was operational. Gas supply was also suspended at Akij and other stations in Tejgaon.
Gas was available at stations in Malibagh, Karwan Bazar’s FDC gate, Paribagh and Moghbazar.
The shortage caused severe congestion at several stations. The queue at the Hajipara pump stretched nearly 1km, while a similar situation was seen in Moghbazar. The queue at Paribagh was comparatively shorter.
CNG driver Ibrahim said he had been moving from one station to another in search of gas.
“Now I am running from one pump to another to find out which ones are supplying gas and which ones are not,” he said.
“Some people said the Jaman pump in Merul Badda was supplying gas, but when I came here, I found that it was not. Now I hear that gas is available at the Hajipara pump, but there is a huge queue,” he added.
“There is no other option. I am going there now. I will wait as long as it takes to get gas,” Ibrahim said.
Another CNG driver, Anwar, said he received only Tk60 worth of gas at the FDC gate shortly before 11:30am after waiting around 2.5 hours.
“How long will we be able to run with this amount of gas? What are we supposed to do now?” he said.
Anwar said he had heard the situation could worsen further, with gas potentially becoming unavailable altogether.
“What will we do? What is the way forward for us? The government should tell us,” he said.
Drivers said the few stations still supplying gas were providing such small quantities that it was barely enough to keep their vehicles running.
Private cars were receiving no more than Tk100 worth of gas, while CNGs were getting a maximum of Tk50-60. Some drivers said they were receiving only Tk20 worth.
Private car driver Sohel Rana said his vehicle received Tk100 worth of gas after a long wait.
“How long can a 1,500cc vehicle run on gas worth Tk100?” he asked.
Private car driver Yunus said there was no certainty about which stations would have gas.
“Most of the pumps are closed. The pumps that are open are not providing more than Tk100 worth of gas,” he said.
“If this continues, those who drive CNGs and private cars on contract will not have anything to eat. We will have to die of hunger. Otherwise, we will have to leave everything and resort to theft and robbery,” Yunus said.
He also expressed frustration over shortages of gas, electricity and other essentials.
At the Akij pump, sales employee Tarek said the station could not supply gas when pressure in the line was too low.
“If there is no gas in the line, how can we supply it? Sometimes some gas comes, but the pressure is very low. Even then, we are trying to supply it. But we are helpless,” he said.
Arman Islam, a sales employee at the Jaman pump, said the station supplied gas whenever it received it.
“We supply gas whenever it comes. But if gas does not come, how can we supply it?” he said.
Drivers said thousands could be left without work if the situation continued, as they depend on gas-powered vehicles for their daily income.
They urged the government to take immediate steps to restore normal gas supplies and prevent the crisis from worsening.

Prosecution concludes arguments against Obaidul Quader, 7 others
item.description:
The prosecution has concluded its arguments against Awami League General Secretary Obaidul Quader and seven other senior leaders of the Awami League, Jubo League and Chhatra League in the July crimes against humanity case at the International Crimes Tribunal.
A three-member judicial panel of International Crimes Tribunal-2, headed by Chairman Justice Nazrul Islam Chowdhury, concluded the arguments on Wednesday.
Chief Prosecutor Md Aminul Islam and Prosecutor Gazi MH Tamim presented the arguments for the prosecution. Lawyers Lokman Howlader and Ishrat Jahan are representing the accused as state-appointed defence counsel.
Journalist Ashraf Kaiser testified before the tribunal on July 26. In his testimony, he described the Awami League's long rule and the July mass uprising.
The first round of testimony in the case concluded on April 27, after which a date was set for arguments. However, the prosecution later sought to record Ashraf Kaiser's testimony, and the tribunal allowed the application. The investigation officer subsequently testified again.
Besides Obaidul Quader, the other accused are Awami League Joint General Secretary AFM Bahauddin Nasim; former state minister for information and broadcasting Mohammad Ali Arafat; Jubo League President Sheikh Fazle Shams Parash and General Secretary Mainul Hossain Khan Nikhil; and Chhatra League President Saddam Hossain and General Secretary Wali Asif Inan. All the accused are absconding.
On January 22, Tribunal-2 ordered the start of the trial after framing charges against the seven accused. On December 18, 2025, the tribunal took cognizance of the formal charges filed by the prosecution. The prosecution began presenting its arguments in the case on August 4.
According to the prosecution, the accused issued coordinated instructions, incited violence and delivered provocative speeches to suppress the July-August movement. They allegedly planned violence through several meetings and called on leaders and activists to take to the streets to resist the movement.
The prosecution further alleged that the accused played roles in armed attacks, severe repression and media control in several areas, resulting in killings, attempted killings and widespread violence across the country.
The prosecution argued that these acts constitute crimes against humanity.

item.title: Salman Shah family allegedly threatened after actor Don’s arrest
item.description:
The family of late actor Salman Shah has allegedly received death threats following the arrest of actor Ashraful Haque Don in the murder case involving the popular actor.
Mohammad Alamgir Kummkum, plaintiff in the case and Salman Shah’s maternal uncle, told reporters on Wednesday that Shahraan, Salman’s brother, had been threatened with death in a Facebook comment.
Kummkum showed journalists a screenshot of the alleged threat after appearing at a Dhaka court for Don’s bail hearing.
He said the threat was posted from a Facebook account named “Shakil Kibria” in the comments of a Facebook Live hosted by a Salman Shah fan named Mamun.
The screenshot showed the comment: “Mamun, tell Neela Chowdhury not to go too far regarding Salman’s death. Otherwise, we will kill Shahraan (Salman Shah’s brother) the way we killed Salman Shah.”
Kummkum said they would file a general diary (GD) with Ramna police over the threat, noting that the Salman Shah murder case was filed with the same police station.
Mamun, who was present at the court, said he was conducting the Facebook Live to call for a human chain by Salman Shah fans when the alleged threat appeared in the comments.
“The comment was later deleted while I was taking a screenshot,” he said.
“We, Salman fans, have been saying that he was murdered. Why are such threats coming after Don’s arrest? This should also be investigated,” Mamun said, urging authorities to bring everyone involved in the case to justice.
Don denied bail
Meanwhile, a Dhaka court rejected Don’s bail petition in the Salman Shah murder case.
On Wednesday afternoon, lawyers including M Faridul Islam and Tarikul Islam Jewel sought bail for Don before Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Mohammad Ehsanul Islam.
Public Prosecutor Omar Faruk Faruqi opposed the petition, while the defence argued that there was no specific allegation against Don in the FIR or arrest warrant and that he was not involved in the alleged incident.
The court rejected the bail petition after hearing both sides.
Earlier, the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) took Don into custody after receiving information from immigration authorities as he was preparing to travel to Saudi Arabia to perform Umrah.
He reportedly had a travel ban in connection with the Salman Shah murder case.
Murder case
Salman Shah died at his residence in Eskaton, Dhaka, on September 6, 1996. His death was initially recorded as a suicide, but a murder case was filed later.
The case has remained under investigation and legal scrutiny for decades.
On October 20, 2025, Kummkum filed a murder case with Ramna police on behalf of Salman’s mother, Neela Chowdhury, against 11 people.
The accused are Samira Haque, her mother Latifa Haque Lucy, businessman Aziz Mohammad Bhai, actor Ashraful Haque Don, David, Javed, Faruk, Ruby, Abdus Sattar, Saju and Rezvi Ahmed alias Farhad.
The latest death-threat allegation has renewed attention on the case, with Salman’s family and fans calling for an investigation to identify the person behind the threat and determine whether they have any connection to the murder case.

item.title: Bomb wrapped in pressure cooker recovered in Savar, defused
item.description:
Police recovered a bomb wrapped in a pressure cooker with scotch tape from a field in Savar’s Sadhapur area early Wednesday and later it was safely defused by the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) bomb disposal unit.
Police and locals said the suspicious object was found inside a blue plastic drum at Ghora Mosque field around 1:30am.
The drum also contained some cloths and a copy of the Quran.
Savar Model Police Station Sub-Inspector Imran Hossain said they initially suspected that the object could be a bomb.
Locals removed the pressure cooker from the drum, placed it in the field and informed police.
Some residents said three unidentified people left the drum at the mosque field at night.
No one has been arrested in this connection yet.
A bomb disposal unit of DMP was informed and its members worked for about four hours before safely defusing the bomb in the afternoon, said the SI.
Earlier on July 30, police recovered another bomb concealed in a pressure cooker from an abandoned bag in front of Joyee General Store in Khejurbagan area of Ashulia.
The bomb disposal unit later defused it through a controlled explosion at a safe location.
Meanwhile, police on Tuesday night detained a youth named Arif Hossain with five crude bombs during a raid in Shyampur area of Hemayetpur in Savar.
On information provided by Arif, the Counter Terrorism and Transnational Crime (CTTC) unit later raided the ground floor of a four-storey building owned by Abdul Jalil and recovered nine more bomb-like objects, several leaflets and a large quantity of bomb-making materials and equipment.
Building owner Abdul Jalil and his daughter Ilma told journalists that a man identifying himself as Abbas Ali rented the apartment on Aug 2.
Savar Model Police Station Officer-in-Charge Saiful Alam said a total of 14 bombs were recovered from Shyampur area.

Five arrested over Pallabi shooting linked to Tk15 lakh drug money dispute
item.description:
Five people, including a notorious drug trader, have been arrested in connection with a shooting incident in the capital’s Pallabi area over the sharing of Tk15 lakh earned from drug sales.
The arrestees are Hamid Khan alias Makhon, drug trader "Lengra" Rubel, Tanzid Ahmed alias Bappa, Parvez and Rabbi.
Police recovered a foreign-made pistol, two rounds of bullets, two magazines, 1,000 Yaba pills and two vehicles allegedly used in drug trading from their possession.
Additional Commissioner (DB) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) Md Shafiqul Islam disclosed the information at a press briefing at the DMP Media Centre on Wednesday afternoon.
He said the shooting took place in front of Emon’s tea stall at Mirpur Section-11 under Pallabi police station around 5:30pm on Aug 7.
Alamgir was shot in the abdomen and head, while a female passerby named Josna sustained a gunshot injury to her leg, he said.
Following a complaint filed by Alamgir’s wife, a case was filed with Pallabi Police Station on charges of attempted murder.
The DB Mirpur Division subsequently launched a shadow investigation.
With the help of video footage and information technology, investigators identified a Toyota Premio car used in the shooting and arrested its registered owner, Hamid Khan alias Makhon, from Pallabi.
During interrogation, Makhon told investigators that although the car was registered in his name, its actual owner is notorious drug trader "Lengra" Rubel.
Based on his information, Rubel’s associates Parvez and Rabbi were arrested from the Kalshi area.
Later, acting on information provided by Parvez and Rabbi, detectives arrested Lengra Rubel and Tanzid Ahmed alias Bappa in an area beside the embankment near Eastern Housing under Rupnagar Police Station.
A foreign-made pistol, two rounds of bullets and two magazines were recovered from them.
During preliminary interrogation, the arrestees said the shooting occurred following a dispute between Alamgir and Lengra Rubel and his associates over the sharing of Tk15 lakh earned from drug sales.
DB officials said Alamgir himself is a listed drug trader and faces several cases in Dhaka, but he is the victim in this case.
Responding to a question, Shafiqul Islam said anyone involved in a crime would be identified as a criminal regardless of their other identity and brought under the law.
He said Rubel faces several cases and investigators are looking into whether he invested money earned from drug trading in different places. If necessary, information will be sent to the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) for possible action under the Money Laundering Prevention Act.
The DB chief said preliminary interrogation also revealed that several other people, including Bappa, were in the vehicle during the shooting. Their identities are not being disclosed for the sake of investigation, and efforts are underway to arrest them.
Apart from the attempted murder case, separate cases under the Arms Act and Narcotics Control Act are being processed.
The arrestees may be taken on remand for further interrogation, while DB operations to arrest others involved in the incident are continuing, Shafiqul said.

item.title: Litton Das cleared for first Australia test
item.description:
Bangladesh wicketkeeper-batter Litton Das has been cleared to play in the first test against Australia in Darwin beginning on Thursday after recovering from a calf injury.

Captain Najmul Hossain Shanto said Litton was 100 per cent fit after completing batting and wicketkeeping drills at Marrara Stadium on Wednesday.

Bangladesh's leading scorer over the past five years will be expected to bat at number five or six.

Shanto said Bangladesh would wait until the morning of the match before finalising their bowling attack but suggested they were leaning toward including a second spinner for the nation's first test in Australia since 2003.

"The surface looks good, I think we (might stick with our) normal combination, like two spinners and three seamers," he told reporters in Darwin on Wednesday.

Bangladesh were bowled out for 54 in a practice match against a Cricket Australia XI in the buildup to the series, raising concerns about their batting.

Shanto put it down to a "bad day" and said Bangladesh had otherwise prepared well to face the hosts.

"They have a world-class bowling attack, but as a team, it is a good opportunity to challenge them," he added.

item.title: Messi pens emotional tribute to late father, questions own future in the game
item.description:
SOCCER-ARGENTINA/MESSI

Lionel Messi said on Wednesday he is having doubts about continuing his career following the death of his father last week.

Messi's father, Jorge, died last week aged 68 at a medical clinic in the Argentine city of Rosario after a long illness.

"I don't know what I'm going to do without you. I don't know how to move forward. I only played football and now I have quite a few doubts about whether I'm going to keep doing it for much longer," Messi wrote in a tribute on Instagram.

"You were by my side from the beginning; there was so little left until the end. Why couldn't you hold on just a little longer so we could finish it together?"

Jorge closely accompanied his son Lionel throughout his career, beginning with his early years at Barcelona. He acted as a crucial pillar of support and, for several years, served as his representative.

The 39-year-old Argentina captain revealed one of the reasons he played in the World Cup, where they finished runners-up to Spain after an extra-time loss in the final, was because it was his father's wish.

"You always asked me to play in the last World Cup and a few days before it started was when you got worse," Messi said.

"It was the first time you weren't going to be at a tournament... Every time a match ended, I would wait and hope for your message. That's when I realised how real the situation was."

During the World Cup, the Argentine captain experienced mixed emotions after scoring a hat-trick in the opening match against Algeria, breaking down in tears while celebrating his first goal.

He later explained that his tears were due to "something unrelated to football" after going through "a few difficult, complicated days."

Messi said he wanted to win the final for his father but he had no energy left to bring home a second World Cup title.

"My legs couldn't go on anymore. This time I tried to push myself beyond my physical limits, but I couldn't. I never felt well... We weren't champions, but you don't know how much we enjoyed every match. Once again, you were right: I had to be there and play it," Messi added.

Despite his grief, the Inter Miami forward pledged to honour his father's memory through parenting his own children.

"I'm going to miss you so much, but you will always be present, especially in the upbringing of my children, because I will teach them and raise them the way you raised me," he said.

item.title: Six senior police officers suspended over absence, negligence
item.description:
The government has suspended six high-ranking police officers for alleged negligence in professional duties, unauthorized absence from work and disobedience of government rules.
The Home Ministry’s Disciplinary-1 Branch issued separate notifications on Wednesday, ordering the suspensions with immediate effect.
The suspended officers are Mohammad Iqbal Hossain, superintendent of police at the Range DIG’s Office in Khulna and former deputy commissioner of police of Wari Division, Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP); Kazi Ashraful Azim, former deputy commissioner of police of Uttara Division, DMP; Biplob Kumar Sarker and Sudip Kumar Chakraborty, both former joint commissioners of police of DMP; Airport Armed Police Battalion (APBN) Additional Superintendent of Police Rajan Kumar Das; and DMP Assistant Commissioner Golam Ruhani.

item.title: Former Chinese premier Zhu Rongji passes away from illness
item.description:
Former Chinese premier Zhu Rongji, whose market reforms helped drive the country’s extraordinary economic rise, died from illness on Wednesday at the age of 97, state media reported.
An obituary jointly issued by China’s top political bodies and carried by Xinhua said he had passed away in Beijing late Wednesday morning “after medical treatment failed to save him.”
Zhu became premier in 1998, and swiftly established a reputation as a hard-hitting free marketeer.
Among his best-known reforms were a broad program to privatize unprofitable state-owned enterprises, the privatization of urban housing and the promotion of home ownership.
Zhu was “an outstanding member of the Communist Party of China, a long-tested and loyal communist fighter,” Xinhua quoted his obituary as saying.
“The life of comrade Zhu Rongji was a life of revolution, a life of struggle, a life of glory,” it said.
“It was a life dedicated wholeheartedly to serving the people, one given to the communist cause. His passing is a major loss for the Party and the country.”

item.title: Presidential election: Nomination papers to be submitted Thursday
item.description:
Nomination papers must be submitted between 10am and 4pm on Thursday to run in the presidential election slated for August 20 next.
The ruling BNP has formally not declared its presidential candidate yet, while the opposition Jamaat-e-Islami-led 11-party alliance has named LDP Chairman Col (retd) Oli Ahmed as its candidate.
However, both the ruling and opposition camps have collected nomination papers for their respective aspirants.
Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin, who is serving as the returning officer of the presidential election, has already convened a meeting of the Members of Parliament (MPs) at the session chamber of the National Parliament on August 20 for voting in the presidential election in line with the Presidential Election Act, 1991.
According to the election schedule announced by the Election Commission on August 06 last, the nomination papers will be scrutinized on August 16 and the last date for withdrawal of candidature is August 18.
Voting will take place from 2:00pm to 5:00pm on August 20 in the session chamber of the National Parliament. A total of 349 MPs are voters in the presidential election. Now a parliamentary seat, Chittagong-4 constituency, remains vacant.
This will be the first presidential election in 35 years, which is going to involve more than one candidate. So, the voting is set to be held in the Presidential election after 1991.
The name of Local Government and Rural Development Minister Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has already surfaced in the media as the BNP’s probable presidential candidate, but people are likely to wait till Thursday to formally know its candidate.
On July 24 last, Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned as President and Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad took charge as the acting president.
According to Article 123(2) of the Constitution, an election to fill the vacant office of the President must be held within 90 days of the post becoming vacant due to resignation.

item.title: Young people face rising hypertension risk in Bangladesh
item.description:
Hypertension and other non-communicable diseases (NCDs) are emerging as growing health concerns among young people in Bangladesh, speakers said at a webinar on Tuesday.
The webinar, titled “Hypertension Risk Among Youth and the Way Forward: Bangladesh Perspective,” was organized by PROGGA (Knowledge for Progress) to mark International Youth Day 2026. It was supported by the Global Health Advocacy Incubator (GHAI) and co-organized by several youth organizations.
Speakers said NCDs account for 71% of all deaths in Bangladesh, with 19% of those deaths occurring prematurely. According to the Bangladesh Bureau of Statistics’ Health and Morbidity Status Survey-2025, hypertension ranks first among the country’s 10 leading diseases.
Data from the Bangladesh NCD STEPS Survey 2018 show that around 12% of people aged 18–39 have hypertension.
Professor Dr Sohel Reza Choudhury, head of the Department of Epidemiology and Research at National Heart Foundation Hospital & Research Institute, said sustainable financing was essential to ensure a regular supply of medicines at primary-level healthcare facilities and reduce premature deaths caused by hypertension.
He said investing in hypertension control could help build a healthier young generation.
Dr Malay Kanti Mridha, professor at BRAC James P Grant School of Public Health, said hypertension could be effectively controlled through evidence-based preventive and curative measures.
Muhammad Ruhul Quddus, Bangladesh country lead at GHAI, said the increase in the health budget was a positive step. He stressed that a significant portion of the additional allocation should be directed toward addressing hypertension and other NCDs.
Mohammad Al Amin, vice president of the Bangladesh Health Reporters Forum (BHRF) and deputy editor of Daily Sun, said the media could play a significant role in ensuring that the government prioritizes NCD control in the allocation and use of the health budget.
Aminul Islam Sujon, consultant at Vital Strategies, also participated in the discussion.
The webinar was chaired by ABM Zubair, executive director of PROGGA, and moderated by Samiha Bintay Kamal, program officer at PROGGA. Representatives of youth organizations and participants from various professional backgrounds attended the webinar.
Speakers stressed the need for immediate action, preventive measures, regular screening and sustainable funding to reduce hypertension risks among young people in Bangladesh.

item.title: Elderly couple, house help found dead at Sylhet house
item.description:
Police recovered the bodies of an elderly couple and their domestic help with their throats slit from a flat of a four stoery building in Sylhet city’s Raynagar residential area on Wednesday.
The deceased were identified as MA Sattar, 82, of Raynagar Rajbari area, his wife Suraiya Begum, 72, and their domestic help Tahmina, 25, of Jallarpar area.
Sylhet Metropolitan Police Commissioner Sarwar Murshed Shamim said a local resident informed him around 9 am that blood was seen flowing from beneath the closed door of the flat owned by Sattar.
Police immediately went to the house and found the three dead with injuries caused by sharp weapons, he said.
Sattar's nephew Munna Mia said he spoke to them around 9am and believed they were killed sometime afterward.
The police commissioner said residents of the building reported hearing screams and shouting in the morning, suggesting that the killings took place around that time.
Crime scene teams from the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) and Criminal Investigation Department (CID) are working at the scene, he said adding that a special police team has been formed to investigate the killings.
Police found wardrobes and cupboards used by the family open, prompting investigators to examine whether any gold ornaments or other valuables have been taken.
“We are investigating whether the incident was a robbery or whether it stemmed from family enmity or a previous dispute,” the police commissioner said.
SMP Media Officer and Additional Deputy Commissioner Md Manzurul Alam said the bodies were sent to the morgue of Sylhet MAG Osmani Medical College Hospital for autopsy after inquest examinations.
Sylhet City Corporation Administrator Abdul Qaiyum Chowdhury visited the scene and spoke with senior police officials following the incident.

item.title: Mango market buzzes in Chapainawabganj as season nears end
item.description:
Mango trading has gained momentum in Chapainawabganj as the season approaches its end, with large numbers of buyers and sellers gathering at major markets across the district.
At Kansat, the district’s largest mango market, trading of late-season and year-round varieties—including Ashwina, BARI-4, BARI-8, Gaurmati, Banana and Katimon—is continuing in full swing.
Thousands of maunds of mangoes are being traded at the market every day, while buyers and sellers remain active despite the season being in its final stage.
Speaking at Kansat market on Tuesday morning, mango grower Hasibul Hasan Babu of Binodpur union in Shibganj upazila said the season was almost over. He said he sold Ashwina mangoes for Tk 3,800 per maund that day, but the price was not satisfactory considering production costs.
Another grower, Monirul Islam of Durlabhpur union, sold BARI-4 mangoes for Tk 7,000 per maund. He said the variety used to fetch a much higher price several years ago. Although prices have improved somewhat recently, growers failed to receive their expected returns at the beginning of the season, he added.
Mango grower and media worker Farhad Ali brought Katimon mangoes to the market and sold them for Tk 6,000 per maund. While he was relatively satisfied with the price, he also expressed disappointment over the overall market situation this year.
Abdur Razzak, a trader involved in online mango trading for a long time, said prices had increased slightly toward the end of the season. However, the market remained unstable throughout the year. Traders like him still managed to make profits, he said.
Grower Abul Hasnat said Shibganj produces more mangoes than the district’s other four upazilas combined. He recalled that Fazli once accounted for nearly 80 percent of the orchards in the area.
In recent years, however, newer varieties such as Banana, Katimon, Amrapali and BARI-4 have increasingly entered the market around the time Fazli mangoes are harvested. As a result, demand for these newer varieties has risen during the late Fazli harvesting period, putting downward pressure on Fazli prices, he said.
Sentu Mia, a mango grower from the Maharajpur area of Sadar upazila, said he had been involved in mango cultivation for nearly two decades.
“Mango farming was profitable about 10 years ago, but growers have struggled to earn satisfactory returns in recent years,” he said. “Production costs have increased, but mango prices have not risen proportionately.”
Abu Taleb, president of the Shibganj Mango Aratdar Association, said the livelihoods of more than 100,000 people in Chapainawabganj were linked to the mango industry.
Production costs are rising every year, but growers are not receiving prices that adequately reflect those increases, he said.
He warned that the district’s mango industry is facing a serious threat and called for the development of mango processing industries, stronger agricultural research and the establishment of a full-fledged mango research institute to ensure the sector’s long-term sustainability.
Meanwhile, mangoes at Kansat, Rohanpur and other markets in the district are currently selling at around Tk 2,000-Tk 5,000 per maund for Ashwina, Tk 8,000-Tk 12,000 for BARI-4, Tk 5,000-Tk 7,000 for Gaurmati, Tk 5,000-Tk 8,000 for Katimon and Tk 12,000-Tk 15,000 for Banana varieties.
According to Atikul Islam, deputy director of the Department of Agricultural Extension in Chapainawabganj, mangoes were cultivated on 37,487 hectares of land in the district this season, with a production target of 458,912 metric tonnes.
He said supplies of several varieties, including Ashwina, Gaurmati, Banana and BARI-4, were continuing even as the mango season entered its final stage.

item.title: Shopping malls, markets and shops ordered to close by 8pm
item.description:
The government has changed the operating hours of shopping malls, markets and shops across the country as part of measures to save electricity.

Under the new schedule, these establishments may remain open from 11:00am to 8:00pm.

The government has also ordered all illuminated billboards to be switched off by 7:00pm. In addition, all decorative lighting has been ordered to remain completely switched off. The new measures came into effect on Wednesday.

The Ministry of Power, Energy and Mineral Resources announced the decisions in an order issued Wednesday evening.

The government has also instructed that ongoing and upcoming trade fairs and cultural events across the country must end by 8:00pm. However, food shops, hospitals, pharmacies and other essential services will remain exempt from the directive, according to the order.

The Energy Ministry said a notification issued on 11 June had allowed shopping malls, markets and shops to remain open until 9:00pm.

Under the new decision, that closing time has now been brought forward to 8:00pm.

It may be noted that on 28 February, the United States and Israel jointly launched attacks on Iran, prompting retaliatory strikes by Iran. The conflict subsequently spread across the Middle East. At one point, the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for fuel supplies, was effectively closed. This led to sharp increases in fuel prices and a worsening energy crisis, whose impact was also felt in Bangladesh.

Against the backdrop of the global energy crisis caused by the conflict in the Middle East, the government reduced the working hours of government and private offices by one hour at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on the night of 2 April.

At the same time, it was decided that shops and shopping malls would close at 6:00pm, a measure that took effect the following day. The closing time was later extended by one hour following a request from shop owners’ associations.

Ahead of Eid-ul-Azha, the government relaxed the operating hours for shops and shopping malls. After Eid, restrictions were tightened again, requiring shops and shopping malls to close at 7:00pm.

However, business owners demanded that shops and shopping malls be allowed to remain open from noon until 10:00pm. In response, the government extended the operating hours on 11 June, allowing them to remain open from 11:00am to 9:00pm.

The government has now revised that decision again, reducing the permitted closing time to 8:00pm.

item.title: Amit: Govt working in every possible way to resolve gas crisis
item.description:
State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Aninda Islam Amit on Wednesday said the government is making every possible effort to ease the gas crisis and improve the power situation.
“We have adopted a strategy since Tuesday evening. Hopefully, the situation will improve soon,” he said while briefing reporters at the Secretariat on the latest situation in the power and energy sectors.
Amit said an LNG cargo is currently waiting at the Floating Storage Regasification Unit (FSRU) operated by Summit Group, as rough weather in the Bay of Bengal has prevented the cargo from being unloaded.
Meanwhile, the FSRU operated by Excelerate Energy is operating at around 50% capacity as one of its two boilers is out of order, he said.
The state minister said the FSRU will need to be shut down for about 72 hours for necessary work to restore it to full capacity. “However, no decision has yet been taken on when the work will begin.”
He said the government is in talks with the FSRU authorities and will consult the business community before taking the decision.
Amit said LNG is currently supplied through the two FSRUs and disruptions at both terminals have affected gas supply.
“If there is not enough supply of gas, it is not possible to supply the required gas to the power plants, which affects electricity generation and supply,” he said.
Regarding Bangladesh’s efforts to import LNG from Malaysia, the state minister said a Bangladeshi delegation has already visited the country following a virtual meeting between the two sides.
“Work is underway on the proposal given by Malaysia. We hope at least one LNG cargo will be available from there,” he said.
The state minister said importing LNG through ISO tanks will require a separate process as the required tanks are not readily available in the market. “This is a medium-term solution, and the government is also working on this,” he said.
Asked about the options being considered to address the current crisis, he said: “We are working on all the options that we have in our hands.”
Amit said energy sector experts discussed the crisis at a seminar at Dhaka Club on Tuesday, while the government is also consulting businessmen and seeking their advice.
Asked whether the government could give people a specific timeframe for improvement in the power situation, he said he was not in a position to provide one.
“The people definitely want to know the message from the government. If I were in a position to give a message, I would have definitely given it,” the state minister said.
“I will just tell you this — we are making a vital effort considering the suffering of the people. I think the people understand this. There is no flaw in our efforts,” he added.
Amit said the government has limited options in dealing with the current situation as natural conditions are beyond its control.
He blamed policy weaknesses of previous government for the current crisis.
The state minister said the previous government had focused on short-term solutions instead of medium- and long-term planning in the power and energy sectors.
“When you adopt the wrong policy, you will have to pay the price at some point. The previous government did not seek any medium-term, long-term, or solutions. They pursued immediate solutions, and today, a crisis has suddenly arisen,” he said.
Amit said such a crisis could have emerged at any time and would eventually have had to be addressed.
He regretted, however, that people are facing the crisis during the summer.

item.title: Journalists protest courtroom access ban at Supreme Court
item.description:
Journalist leaders have alleged that barring media workers from Supreme Court courtrooms violates the constitution, urging the chief justice to immediately restore their access.
They warned of tougher programs if the restriction is not lifted.
They made the remarks on Wednesday at a sit-in organized by the Law Reporters Forum (LRF), an organization of journalists covering law, justice, constitutional affairs and human rights. The program was held in front of the Supreme Court’s main gate.
Journalist leaders said journalists have been denied access to various courtrooms of the Supreme Court, including the Appellate Division, since January 7.
They said the restriction has prevented journalists from directly observing proceedings in pending cases and collecting news.
Nurul Kabir, president of the Editors Guild and editor of New Age, said journalists were protesting an unjust decision.
“It is extremely unfortunate. Following a bloody mass uprising, the goal was to establish democracy, democratic rights and justice in society. At such a time, court proceedings should have been made accessible to people through the media,” he said.
“We are seeing the highest level of the judiciary depriving people of their right to information.”
Kabir said the media had stood by the judiciary whenever previous governments attempted to undermine the courts or judicial system.
“When the highest court itself obstructs the media from carrying out that responsibility, questions arise about the democratic commitment of the judiciary’s leadership,” he said.
He said conducting proceedings in open court is a constitutional obligation.
“If rights guaranteed by the Constitution are violated, the highest authority of the judiciary is responsible for protecting them. If that very institution violates those rights, it is sad, unfortunate and shameful,” Kabir said.
He said the Editors Guild hoped the Supreme Court would not violate the Constitution by restricting access to open court proceedings.
“We sought a meeting with the chief justice to discuss the matter but did not get one. I hope the chief justice and other judges will understand its importance. They must clearly understand that the measures being taken against news gathering are contrary to the Constitution of Bangladesh,” he said.
Dhaka Journalists Union President Shahidul Islam said people turn to courts as their last resort when their rights are violated or they become victims of injustice.
“But when the court itself deprives people of their rights, where will they go?” he asked.
“If our rights are not restored through this peaceful program, we will take to the streets.”
Addressing the chief justice, Shahidul said: “You know that after August 5, 2024, the country’s chief justice fled, the Khatib of the National Mosque fled and many judges fled. We do not want to go down that path. Establish the right to information. Otherwise, we will have to take tougher programs. Do not force us in that direction.”
Dhaka Reporters Unity President Abu Saleh Akon questioned why journalists were being prevented from entering courtrooms.
“What happens inside the courtroom that the nation cannot know? Why are journalists being barred from entering the court? This creates suspicion among the people,” he said.
Akon said journalists had witnessed “dictated verdicts” being delivered during the previous regime, some of which resulted in executions.
“We have fought for freedom of speech and freedom of writing for years. We will not accept any obstruction to our writing or professional duties,” he said.
He said several former judges were now serving prison terms over alleged misconduct, while others had fled the country.
“We do not want to see such examples in the future. I want freedom of speech and freedom of writing to be further strengthened under this chief justice,” Akon said.
“If that does not happen, we may block roads in our next program. At that point, you will not be able to hold us responsible.”
He also urged the government to discuss journalists’ professional rights with the chief justice and ensure they can perform their duties without obstruction.
“Otherwise, journalist organizations will launch a united movement with the Law Reporters Forum,” he said.
Bangladesh Crime Reporters Association General Secretary MM Badshah, Reporters Against Corruption President Shafi Uddin Ahmed, Reporters Forum for Election and Democracy President Kazi Emad Uddin Jebel, former LRF president and Ittefaq Executive Editor Saleh Uddin, RTV Head of News and former DRU president Ilias Hossain, former LRF president M Badi-Uz-Zaman and others expressed solidarity with the LRF’s demands.
In his concluding remarks, LRF President Muhammad Yasin said the forum would soon announce a programme to enter the Appellate Division courtroom if its demands were not met.
The programme was moderated by LRF General Secretary Arafat Munna.
More than 200 journalists, including LRF executive committee members, attended the sit-in.

item.title: Zahid: Efforts underway to end red tape
item.description:
Social Welfare Minister Dr AZM Zahid Hossain has stressed the need to make and implement government decisions quickly to achieve the SDGs, saying efforts are being made to speed up bureaucratic activities.
“Efforts are underway to end red tape. All relevant stakeholders should be brought together at one table to make quick decisions and implement those,” he told a session at the national conference on SDGs at the Bangladesh-China Friendship Conference Center in the capital on Wednesday.
Noting that Bangladesh currently ranks 110th in terms of implementing the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), Zahid said there is very little time left to implement SDGs so that “we have to move forward rapidly now”.
Turning to BNP government’s target, he said the government’s goal is to build a Bangladesh where the benefits of development are not limited to cities or people with financial means.
People with disability, as well as disadvantaged people living on footpaths and at railway stations, will also receive equal importance.
The minister said the government eyes to build such a Bangladesh where no one neglects anyone else.
Highlighting various government programmes for the education, skills development and rehabilitation of people with special needs, Zahid said it would not be enough to limit their opportunities to formal education.
They must also be provided with technical training, opportunities to acquire advanced skills and rehabilitation support, he said.
Zahid said an initiative has been taken to introduce mobile vehicles to provide physiotherapy and speech therapy services to people in remote areas.
There are plans to extend these services to the upazila level, with a target of implementing the programme within the next three years, he added.
Regarding daycare services, Zahid, also minister for women and children affairs, said daycare facilities would be expanded at the district and upazila levels.
The government plans to expand the services according to demand rather than keeping them concentrated only in cities, he said adding that in particular, efforts are being made to establish daycare facilities through partnerships with the private sector for the children of women working in the garment industry.
The minister said the government is planning to develop skilled caregivers and sees the caregiving sector as an opportunity not only for domestic employment but also for exporting skilled workers to the international labour market.
Different types of caregivers are needed for children, people with special needs, sick people and the elderly, he said.
Developing skilled caregivers could help meet domestic demand while also creating opportunities for overseas employment and increasing remittances, said Zahid.
The minister also spoke about plans to expand training programmes at the upazila level to develop the skills of women and young people.
Training will be provided in areas including livestock and poultry, handicrafts, beautification, tailoring, mobile phone repair, plumbing, welding and automobile maintenance, he added.
Zahid said there are also plans to provide necessary equipment and seed money after training so that trainees can become self-employed and entrepreneurs.
Regarding the Family Card programme, the minister said beneficiaries are not being selected on the basis of political affiliation.
“It has not been considered which political party anyone belongs to. The goal is to ensure universal access to benefits,” he said.
As money will be transferred directly through banks and mobile financial services, there will be no opportunity for middlemen to become involved in the programme, he said.
Prime Minister’s Adviser and Prime Minister Office (PMO)’s spokesperson Mahdi Amin and BNP Standing Committee member Begum Selima Rahman, MP and Madhabi Marma, MP, also spoke with Dr Debapriya Bhattacharya, convener of the Citizens’ Platform for SDGs, in the chair.

item.title: Two CUET students drown in campus pond
item.description:
Two students of Chittagong University of Engineering and Technology (CUET) drowned in a pond on the university campus in Raozan upazila of Chittagong on Wednesday.
The deceased were identified as Arnab Chando, 22, a student of the Department of Computer Science and Engineering, and Shanto Dev, 23, a student of the Department of Civil Engineering.
According to fellow students, the two went to the pond adjacent to Kabi Kazi Nazrul Islam Hall at noon to bathe after playing football. They drowned while swimming in the middle of the pond.
Arnab was rescued about 20 minutes after he went missing, while Shanto was rescued around 45 minutes later.
They were taken to Evercare Hospital in Chittagong, where doctors declared them dead.
CUET Student Welfare Director Prof Saiful Islam said the bodies were kept at the hospital.
The families of the deceased were informed and further action will be taken according to their wishes, he said.
The incident comes less than two weeks after another CUET student, Arnab Saha, 22, drowned in the same pond on July 28.
Arnab Saha was a student of the 2021-22 academic session in the Department of Mechanical Engineering.

item.title: Kaptai Lake choked by water hyacinth, disrupts boat movement
item.description:
A massive accumulation of water hyacinth has severely disrupted boat movement along nearly a one-kilometre stretch of Kaptai Lake near Kaptai Jetty in Rangamati, creating serious difficulties for passengers, boat operators and fish traders.
The floating weeds, carried by currents from different parts of the lake, have piled up around the jetty, obstructing engine-run boats and other watercraft. During a visit to the area on Tuesday, large sections of the Kaptai Inland Water Transport Terminal, BFDC Platoon Ghat and surrounding waterways were found covered with dense layers of water hyacinth.
Many boats, including fish-laden vessels, were struggling to reach the jetty. Boat operators said they were being forced to spend significantly more time and effort navigating through the vegetation. Although the weeds are occasionally cleared, fresh masses quickly drift into the area and accumulate again.
Passengers travelling to Bilaichhari—Md Osman, Swinu Marma and Ananda Tanchangya—said the first one-kilometre stretch after leaving Kaptai Jetty had become particularly difficult to cross.
“Sometimes it takes nearly an hour to cross this short stretch,” they said.
Boat operators Md Main Uddin, Md Zakir Hossain and Nur Nabi said water hyacinth had become the biggest obstacle to navigation around the jetty. According to them, a journey that normally takes about five minutes can now take up to an hour because of the dense vegetation.
They also said the weeds frequently become entangled with boat propellers, causing damage almost every day. As a result, operators have to bear additional repair and maintenance costs.
Kaptai Fish Traders Association President Belal Hossain and General Secretary Nabi Hossain said water hyacinth does not usually grow in such large quantities around Kaptai Jetty. Instead, currents carry large amounts of the vegetation from areas including Bilaichhari, Juraichhari, Baghaichhari, Barkal and Naniarchar before it becomes trapped around the jetty.
The accumulation has also created problems for fish traders. Fish-laden boats are struggling to reach the jetty, making the loading and unloading of fish increasingly difficult.
The traders attributed the situation partly to water discharge from the Kaptai Hydroelectric Power Station during electricity generation. They said the resulting current carries water hyacinth downstream towards the jetty.
According to them, authorities at the power station used large trawlers in previous years to clear the vegetation. They urged the authorities to undertake an immediate removal operation this year.
Mahmud Hasan, manager of the Karnaphuli Hydroelectric Power Station, said water-hyacinth removal operations are conducted around this time every year. However, he acknowledged that permanently solving the problem is difficult because fresh vegetation continues to drift downstream.
Local residents, passengers, fish traders and boat operators have called for the immediate removal of the accumulated weeds and the introduction of a modern, long-term management system to keep passenger and goods transportation on Kaptai Lake operational and reduce the risk of accidents.

item.title: At least 44 drown after ferry overturns on Zimbabwe’s Lake Kariba
item.description:
Search and rescue operations continued Wednesday after a government passenger ferry capsized on Zimbabwe’s Lake Kariba, claiming at least 44 lives, authorities said.
A witness told AFP that after the ferry sank in rough weather on Tuesday bodies could be seen in the water as rescuers tried to reach the vessel, which was entirely overturned.
Passengers had pleaded with the driver to turn back in the rough waters, local media quoted a survivor as saying.
The civil protection unit (CPU) said overnight that 77 people had been rescued and 15 bodies retrieved from the Rural Infrastructure Development Agency (Rida) ferry.
The Zimbabwe Republic Police updated the toll later Wednesday, saying on X: “The ZRP informs the public that the death toll in the Kariba RIDA boat accident is now 44.”
It is one of the worst recorded passenger boat disasters on the lake, which is on the border with Zambia and more than 300 kilometers (185 miles) northeast of the capital, Harare.
The vessel transports people between the northern town of Kariba and islands and fishing villages around the vast stretch of water, the largest man-made lake in the world.
It provided a vital link for villagers and traders from rural areas to the Kariba commercial hub.
A survivor told the ZBC broadcaster that passengers had asked the driver of the ferry to turn back because of the choppy conditions but he refused.
The vessel may also have been damaged because it was taking on water, said the woman, whose name was not provided.
“We went ahead with some water in the boat while the waves were also getting stronger and rocking the boat. We pleaded with him to phone the captain but he said to us we were not in a position to tell him what to do,” she said.
The ferry had the capacity for 90 people but was carrying 114 adult passengers, five crew members and an unspecified number of children when it went down, the CPU said.
Video taken soon after the accident showed a helicopter hovering over the upturned ferry as an assortment of boats took part in the rescue. Bodies and items floated nearby.
The witness, Maxton Kanhema, told AFP that the boat left in the morning in bad weather and may have been hit by a wave, causing its engines to switch off.
“When we were in the waters, then you could see a distress sign and then boats that were close by responded,” said Kanhema, who was on a small boat which attended the scene on Tuesday afternoon.
A national park provided a helicopter to help in the rescue effort alongside bigger boats and divers from the local area and the army, he said.
“People were in distress... there were bodies in the water and it was a sad situation to witness. Those that could be rescued were rescued,” he said.
In a message of condolence, President Emmerson Mnangagwa said he had declared the accident a national disaster.
“This tragedy has exposed serious deficiencies in our maritime capabilities which we have to address immediately so that our places of recreation do not become death traps to the innocent,” he said.
A specialized aquatic rescue unit was airlifted to the area to aid in the search and two funeral parlours were engaged to collect the bodies, the CPU said.

item.title: Trump says US will ‘keep’ Hormuz strait control
item.description:
President Donald Trump on Wednesday said the United States is in control of the strategic Strait of Hormuz and will “keep it.”
“The USA has total control over the Strait of Hormuz. I THINK WE WILL KEEP IT!” Trump wrote on his Truth Social platform. “Our Naval Blockade is being called, by everyone, ‘A WALL OF STEEL,’ and there is nothing Iran can do about it.”
Trump has repeatedly claimed the United States controls the strait, which is vital for the flow of energy and other commodity shipping through the Middle East.
However, Iran says it effectively controls much of the waterway and intends to impose a toll system in response to the US war launched by Trump on February 28.
Late Tuesday, Trump told reporters: “We have total control over the Hormuz Strait right now. They don’t have control. We have total control. We own it.”
US and Israeli forces have heavily bombed Iran’s military and killed a swath of the country’s leadership so far in the nearly six-month war, launched initially with goals including forcing Tehran to abandon its nuclear power program and regime change.
Iran has resisted with missile attacks on US bases in the region, Israel and targets in US-allied Gulf countries.
Its most effective response has been to strike shipping in Hormuz, effectively snarling the trade route, rattling the world economy.
With his political popularity sinking at home ahead of the November midterm congressional elections, Trump has backed off threats to escalate the war in search of a decisive victory.
That leaves the war in a standoff.
However, the Republican says that the United States is prepared to focus on blockading Iranian ports in a strategy that he told Axios was “low-keying.”
“We are only semi-negotiating with them. We are just watching Iran with its huge inflation and the fact they have no money,” Trump told Axios on Sunday.
